payload.claim: `bare = subject == path` infers whether a `removes` entry was a bare path (no `:name`) by comparing the resolved subject to the path string, instead of checking whether the entry actually contained a colon. If an author writes an entry like `pkg/thing.py:pkg/thing.py` where the declared name happens to equal the path string, `bare` becomes `True` even though the entry explicitly named a subject, and the following `if bare and consumed_path == path` branch at line 738 will then match any reader whose `consumes` path half equals that path regardless of its declared name, producing a clash the spec's rule ('The removed entry is a bare path...') does not call for. No test in the diff exercises an entry where name equals path, so this misclassification is not caught.
